text.p: Sundstrand Corp said Friday it expects earnings this year of $2.65 to $2.85 a share, excluding previously announced restructuring charges and any future share repurchases.
"We expect 1997 to be a good year for Sundstrand and project that sales will increase between 10 percent and 15 percent," Robert Jenkins, president, said in a statement.
For 1996, Sundstrand's sales from ongoing businesses were $1.52 billion, and earnings before charges were $140 million, or $2.30 a share.

Jenkins said that in addition to the previously disclosed acquisition of the remaining interest in its Auxiliary Power International Corp joint venture, Sundstrand has acquired electrical load management technology from Leach International Corp.

"Although both acquisitions are expected to be very good for the company, each will have a slightly dilutive impact in 1997," he said. "In addition, we will be investing in strategic initiatives, which are expected to adversely affect profitability in 1997."
He said these initiatives should begin to provide benefits as early as 1998, with even greater benefits by the year 2000.

In 1996, net earnings before restructuring charges were up 14 percent from a year earlier, on a six percent increase in sales from ongoing businesses. Earnings per share grew 17 percent, excluding restructuring.

Sundstrand repurchased 361,074 shares in the quarter, for a total of 1,372,074 in 1996. The company has repurchased 297,112 shares thus far in 1997 and intends to repurchase shares on an opportunistic basis.
